items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 27 at 10:44AM AKDT until October 27 at 2:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Dense fog. Visibility one quarter mile or less at times.

* WHERE...Eielson AFB and Salcha, Fairbanks Metro Area, and
Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.
items.areas: Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Fairbanks Metro Area
items.instruction:

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 27 at 10:44AM AKDT until October 29 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp and Windy Pass.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Wednesday to 7 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree

items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 27 at 7:02AM AKDT until October 27 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Slick
roads due to black ice.

* WHERE...Anchorage.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT today.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility. Below
freezing temperatures may lead to frost on bridges and roadways.
items.instruction:
A dense fog advisory means visibilities will frequently be reduced to
less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 6:19AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
have caused portions of that snowfall to melt creating many slushy
areas of melting snow and pooling water. Overnight low
temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning are expected to
fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will allow much of this
slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very likely Wednesday
morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles freeze. Areas

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 4:20AM AKDT until October 28 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water levels are expected to peak Tuesday
evening.

* WHERE...Baldwin Peninsula and Northern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts will peak around 45 to 55 mph
out of the south/southeast. Water levels remain slightly above
normal, but slowly lower through the end of the week after
Tuesday.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.description:

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
